Name: SIMHATEL
Description:
Application Of Robotics & AI in Industries
Electronics & Information Technology had driven the 3rd Industrial Revolution resulting in the automation of Manufacturing, space exploration, and all other such industries.

The endless possibilities of the 4th Industrial Revolution are accelerated by the exponential innovations in the fields of Robotics, Drones, Autonomous Vehicles, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), Machine Learning (ML), Smart Sensors, 3D Printing, Clean Energy and Energy Storage.

A new alternate robotic inspection mechanism called as NCM (Non-Contact Condition Monitoring) system based on robotic agents (AGV &UAV), non-contact sensors, and AI platforms are introduced to complement and overcome the shortcomings of the conventional inspection of the buried pipelines by ILI (In-Line Inspection) tool.

The capability of predicting the yet to happen future anomalies in the pipeline is not possible with the conventional inspection methods. So, a novel predictive maintenance mechanism based on Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) for inspection and management of the buried metallic pipes are also integrated.

Name: Systel Energy Solutions (India) Pvt Ltd
Description:
Systel Energy Solutions helps manufacturing plants across India and Asia Pacific cut compressed air energy costs by 20–40% — through ISO 11011-compliant audits, real-time monitoring, and digitization solutions that are measured, documented, and verifiable.

Compressed air is the most expensive utility on your plant floor — often 10–30% of your total electricity bill — and the most ignored. 25–40% is wasted on leaks, artificial demand, pressure drops, and oversized compressors running at part-load. We find it, fix it, and prove the savings stick.

What we do:
• Compressed air audits (ISO 11011): baseline Specific Power Consumption, map leaks ultrasonically, model demand vs. supply, and deliver a prioritized savings roadmap with payback under 18 months.

Name: ICON AUTOMATION
Description:
ICON AUTOMATION is the "Industrial automation optimizes processes, boosts efficiency, and enhances safety by integrating control systems, robotics, and advanced technologies. It's revolutionizing manufacturing and beyond."

Control Systems: Industrial automation relies on control systems to monitor and manage machinery and processes. These systems can range from simple relay-based logic to complex computer-based systems using programmable logic controllers (PLCs), distributed control systems (DCS), or industrial PCs.

Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs): PLCs are specialized computers used to control industrial processes and machinery. They are programmed using ladder logic or other programming languages to execute specific tasks, such as controlling motors, valves, and other equipment
Robotics: Industrial robots are increasingly being used in automation to perform tasks such as assembly, welding, painting, and material handling. These robots are equipped with sensors, actuators, and control systems to perform their designated tasks with precision and efficiency.

Human-Machine Interface (HMI): HMIs provide operators with a graphical interface to monitor and control industrial processes. HMIs can range from simple push-button panels to sophisticated touchscreen displays that provide real-time data visualization and diagnostics.

Communication Protocols: Industrial automation systems often rely on various communication protocols to exchange data between different components. Common protocols include Modbus, Profibus, Ethernet/IP, and DeviceNet.

Integration with IT Systems: With the advent of Industry 4.0 and the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT), there is a growing trend towards integrating industrial automation systems with IT systems such as enterprise resource planning (ERP) software, manufacturing execution systems (MES), and cloud-based platforms for advanced analytics and predictive maintenance.

Name: The Mobile Robots
Description:
Mobile Robots are automatic machines that is capable of locomotion. 

Mobile Robots can replace humans with simple, easy to operate devices that do the same job for less cost, hence a fast ROI. Mobile robots are generally controlled by software and use sensors and other gear to identify their surroundings. Mobile robots combine the progress in artificial intelligence with physical robotics, which allows them to navigate their surroundings.

We are here to help you understand the next generation Mobile Robots. We publish News, Trends, Applications, Courses and Jobs related Mobile Robotics space.

Mobile robots have the capability to move around in their environment and are not fixed to one physical location. Mobile robots can be "autonomous" (AMR - autonomous mobile robot) which means they are capable of navigating an uncontrolled environment without the need for physical or electro-mechanical guidance devices. Alternatively, mobile robots can rely on guidance devices that allow them to travel a pre-defined navigation route in relatively controlled space (AGV - autonomous guided vehicle). By contrast, industrial robots are usually more-or-less stationary, consisting of a jointed arm (multi-linked manipulator) and gripper assembly (or end effector), attached to a fixed surface.

The range of potential applications for mobile robots is enormous. It includes agricultural robotics applications, routine material transport in factories, warehouses, office buildings and hospitals, indoor and outdoor security patrols, inventory verification, hazardous material handling, hazardous site cleanup, underwater applications, and numerous military applications.

Customization is one of the principles ITEC believes in. This drives us to develop many innovative designs during our 25 years of span in the industry. Some of them are; the diaphragm seals for very low pressure applications, external zero adjustment facility in pressure, differential pressure instruments, which helps our customer the easy correction of reading in dampened gauges, differential pressure measurement up to 40 bar with single side static up to 400 bar, etc.


In 1990s’ ITEC started offering the OEM services to some of the major industries across Europe; which ITEC still offer to its valued Customers, and started offering from India factory from mid of 2014. Managing a fragmented supply chain is the biggest bottleneck in custom automation. Coordinating between a mechanical design bureau, a fabrication shop, and a separate software integration team causes delays, budget overruns, and finger-pointing.

Mechanical Design & Prototyping: We de-risk complex kinematics by utilizing our in-house 3D printing farm to physically validate custom mechanisms before any metal is cut.

Precision Fabrication & Assembly: We physically build, route pneumatics, and assemble heavy-duty structural frames and precision tooling on our shop floor.

Controls & PLC Integration: We don't just build the hardware. We wire the panels, program the PLCs, and integrate sensors to deliver fully intelligent, automated cells.

SCADA & Predictive Maintenance: We integrate advanced SCADA architectures to provide real-time OEE dashboards and remote diagnostics. We design for maximum uptime, allowing for data-driven, predictive maintenance rather than reactive downtime.

Turnkey Deployment: Whether you need robust rotary indexing tables for automotive parts or high-precision test jigs for electronic manufacturing, every system undergoes rigorous cycle testing before deployment.

We ensure global compliance and reliability by engineering around Tier-1 components (e.g., SMC/Festo, SKF, Siemens).

SIPOAL - B IoT-based fully Automatic Lubricator enabled with Bluetooth to control and monitor remotely.

SIPOAL - L, IoT based fully Automatic Lubricator enabled with long-range wireless technology (network range upto 10 Kms) to control and monitor remotely & lively.

* Remote control and monitor thru smartphone/computer.

Name: Axiom Robotics & Automation
Description:
Axiom's mission is to drive your productivity by closing the automation gaps on your factory floor. We design and build complete robotic systems in-house — from the parts up to the finished machine — so every cell fits the way you already build, instead of forcing your work to fit the robot.

From collaborative machine tending and robotic welding to machine-vision inspection, precision machining, assembly, palletising and autonomous mobile robots moving material across the plant, Axiom automates the processes that decide your throughput — making them more efficient, more reliable and more resilient, shift after shift. Whether you need a single cell or a full production line, we engineer it around the operation you already run.

Because we own the whole stack — tooling, controls, software and commissioning — our robots adapt as your site grows, and every system is engineered to CE and ISO 10218 safety standards. Where it helps, Axiom OS gives your team one interface to program, monitor and re-task any robot brand from a single screen, with no vendor lock-in.

We are also OEM-agnostic: we specify the best robot for the job and act as the integration partner and route to market for robot makers, turning their hardware into deployed, supported solutions. For you, that means one point of contact for robots from any brand.

Our goal is to optimise your production with minimal integration effort — lifting output from the very first cycle while significantly reducing cost and downtime. We start on your floor, not in a proposal: understand, plan, build, integrate, and support long past go-live.

Every enquiry reaches a real engineer within one business day, and your first on-site assessment is free.

Let's build it Better.

Name: International Society of Automation - Gujarat Section
Description:
The International Society of Automation (ISA) is a non-profit professional association founded in 1945 to create a better world through automation. ISA advances technical competence by connecting the automation community to achieve operational excellence and is the trusted provider of standards-based foundational technical resources, driving the advancement of individual careers and the overall profession. ISA develops widely used global standards; certifies professionals; provides education and training; publishes books and technical articles; hosts conferences and exhibits; and provides networking and career development programs for its members and customers around the world.

ISA created the ISA Global Cybersecurity Alliance (isa.org/ISAGCA) to advance cybersecurity readiness and awareness in manufacturing and critical infrastructure facilities and processes. The Alliance brings end-user companies, automation and control systems providers, IT infrastructure providers, services providers, system integrators, and other cybersecurity stakeholder organizations together to proactively address growing threats.

ISA owns Automation.com, a leading online publisher of automation-related content, and is the founding sponsor of The Automation Federation (automationfederation.org), an association of non-profit organizations serving as “The Voice of Automation.” Through a wholly-owned subsidiary, ISA bridges the gap between standards and their implementation with the ISA Security Compliance Institute (isasecure.org) and the ISA Wireless Compliance Institute (isa100wci.org).

Name: Pilo Foundation
Description: We are operating at a very new and completely different concept. Here we are having the BIS water purification plant and chilling units established at different location in Delhi/NCR area. From these BIS plants, the purified water is filled in the Steel Insulated Tankers with the capacity of 4000 liters each and then this water is carried to Fixed Units set up at central location to the all metro stations in a particular area. The insulated Tanker helps us to keep water chilled for long duration. We run the process in two shifts i.e. morning shift and afternoon shift. Early morning, the Mobile Units having a capacity of 500 liters each, are filled with water at the Fixed Unit. These mobile Units are then placed at their respective metro stations for serving water to every individual. The same process is carried out in afternoon shift also. If water is completely consumed then the Tanker helps the mobile units for refilling it so as to provide the continuous service without any obstruction. After completion for the day, all Mobile Units are brought back to Fixed Units for maintenance purpose.

Name: Ecotech Elevators Italy
Description:
ABOUT – ECOTECH ITALY
Sicor ITALY and sharp working with Ecotech in India, a unique story going through the decades and travelling towards the future.
It was 1981, in fact, when the ambitious project became tangible matter: what had previously been imagined on paper, became a real business! A company thought of in a different way, set up in a strategic territory: headquartered in Rovereto, in the north-eastern Italian province of Trento, sheltered by the Alps, located within a few dozen miles away from the Austrian border.....an Italian brand with sheer determination to succeed abroad. Thanks to SICOR’s new ownership in 2005, the company’s business began to soar under the positive force of the new management, immediately specializing in the elevator sector, with the manufacturing of rope traction systems for the vertical transport of people and goods.
To start with, SICOR means 200 employees and an annual turnover of 60 million Euros.....with more than 20 million Euros invested in research projects: an ambitious, far sighted vision.
A simple rule: “to be and provide for what the market demands, being steadily focussed on customer care“. With this view, SICOR supplies a wide range of traditional gearboxes, as well as gear-less motors for elevators, designed to provide safe, technically advanced solutions for any type of lifting platforms

ECOTECH ITALY – THE SICOR PRODUCTION
Sicor gearbox production range covers nominal loads up to 5,500 kg in 1:1 roping, speeds up to 4m/s with traction pulleys ranging from 320 to 885mm.
In addition, Sicor gearless motor production range covers loads up to 4,000 kg in 2:1 roping, speeds up to 4 m/s, with more speed range on request and traction pulleys ranging from 120 to 670mm. Moreover, since 2015 the gearless range has been implemented with motors featuring a central pulley for elevators with sling car frames and with reduced distance between guide rails and overheads.
